summary: A --select projection that matches no field anywhere must fail loudly (exit 2, plus a diagnostic naming the fields that were available) instead of falling through to the untouched payload.
reason: The projection helper treated a total miss as 'nothing to filter' and returned the full response with exit 0, so a mis-rooted path — --select results.tracks.items.name, where paths are relative to the data and not to the {meta, results} envelope — read as success while emitting exactly the payload --select exists to avoid. The failure is silent and expensive: a caller piping to jq sees an empty result and retries, and an agent pays for the whole response every time. A partial match is still honoured; only a total miss is an error, so legitimate mixed selections are unaffected. The available-field list is capped so the diagnostic cannot become its own token burn on a deeply wrapped payload. The diagnostic itself rides the normal envelope on stdout, because available_fields is data a caller wants to parse; a one-line prose explanation goes to stderr alongside it, so the CLI's documented 'errors on stderr' contract still holds for a human who typed the wrong path.
validated_outcome: Live: --select results.tracks.items.name on spotify-web-search went from a 1750-byte payload with exit 0 to a bounded diagnostic with exit 2; --select tracks.items.name still projects normally. The three existing filterFields cases that asserted the silent-empty contract were updated to the new one.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Fail-on-total-miss for --select in the shared projection template, so every printed CLI reports a mis-rooted path instead of returning the full payload with exit 0.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: The silent passthrough is generator-template behavior, not Spotify-specific; this local patch should be superseded once the template owns it.
